land.text: the Cape taken by the British in January 1806 after the Battle of Blaauwberg

successors.note: Capitulation 8-18 January 1806; the Dutch formally ceded sovereignty on 13 August 1814 (infobox 'Official relinquishment'). The first British occupation (1795-1803) is the same hand-over in the other direction.

capitals.name: Cape Town (Kaapstad), Castle of Good Hope
capitals.note: Infobox: Castle of Good Hope (1st), Kaapstad (2nd); no years given. Coordinates are the researcher's.

correction.text: Cape Town and the Castle of Good Hope, the re-supply point built in 1652

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1653 but the infobox gives 'Established: 6 April 1652'. The settlement of the first year was the fort and the farms near Table Bay (the page: 'earmarked two areas near the Liesbeek River for farming purposes in 1657'), so a 25 km circle at Cape Town is drawn.

minus.text: Gorée and the Cap-Vert coast of Senegal, held by the Dutch West India Company, not the Cape

correction.text: the Cape settlement and its farmland, without Gorée and the Cap-Vert coast

keyframe_review.note: 1653-1720, 28,876 km2. The shape is the Cape (90 cells) plus 12-14 cells in Senegal at Gorée and the Cap-Vert coast. The Gorée page has Gorée under the Dutch West India Company (1621-1663 and 1664-1677) and 'France 1677-1758', never under the VOC Cape, so the Senegal cells are removed for all 1653-1720. The Cape part is kept: the page gives no frontier before the 1745 Swellendam magistracy (unverified for its extent; the infobox area 145,000 km2 has no year and is for the colony's last phase).

correction.text: the shape unchanged, for 1721-1730 only: the Cape plus the Dutch factory at Delagoa Bay

keyframe_review.note: 1721-1733, 27,031 km2: the Cape plus 5 cells at Delagoa Bay (Maputo), correct for the years the Dutch held the bay. The Delagoa Bay page: fort Lijdzaamheid built 1720, governed from the Cape 'since April 1721', 'in December 1730 the settlement was abandoned'. The shape stands for 1721-1730; 1731-1733 is the Cape alone (new keyframe 1731). The Senegal cells of the 1653 shape are already gone in this shape.

correction.text: the Cape without Delagoa Bay (abandoned December 1730)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the December 1730 abandonment of Delagoa Bay the Dutch hold the Cape alone until Cliopatria's next step in 1734.

1734-1768, 57,587 km2 (the Western Cape west of about 22 E). Unverified: the page opened dates no frontier step in 1734; the 1745 Swellendam magistracy falls inside the span. Infobox area (145,000 km2, no year) cannot be compared.

1769-1787, 156,768 km2, adds 381 cells (Western Cape, Northern Cape). The page dates no frontier step in 1769 (it says only that the Gamtoos River 'was declared the eastern frontier' without a year), so the step stays unverified. The shape stands for 1769-1779; from November 1780 the Great Fish River boundary of the 1788 shape applies (new keyframe 1780).

correction.text: the Cape to the Great Fish River, the shape Cliopatria begins in 1788

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In November 1780, Van Plettenberg declared that the eastern border of the Cape colony was the entire length of the Great Fish river' (the page adds that the VOC had demarcated the river in 1779). Cliopatria's 1788 shape (278,665 km2) is the Cape to the Fish River, so it is used from 1780; the Graaff Reinet magistracy of 1786 lies inside it.

1788-1793, 278,665 km2 (the Cape to the Great Fish River incl. Graaff Reinet district). Infobox area 145,000 km2 (no year): ratio 1.92, inside the factor of two; the infobox is probably the settled colony, the shape includes the Karoo and Bushmansland grazing. The Fish River line (Xhosa Wars page: November 1780) fits the shape's eastern edge.

1794-1795, the same 278,665 km2 shape. The VOC colony ends in 1795 with the British landing (infobox 'First British occupation: 7 August 1795'); the Graaff-Reinet district proclaimed a republic in 1795 (ledger).

1803-1804, 278,665 km2, the same Cape shape. 'Britain ceded the Cape back to the Batavian Republic on 1 March 1803'; Cliopatria's British Cape Colony row also draws this land in 1803-1805 (the british-cape-colony dossier removes it). Merged into this dossier because the two Cliopatria rows share Wikidata Q4807130 and the Dutch Cape Colony article treats 1652-1806 as one colony.

1805, the same shape. The Batavian colony ends with the British capture of January 1806 (infobox 'British occupation 8-18 January 1806'); Cliopatria ends the row in 1805, the state's last year here is 1806 (January).

region.text: Cape Town and the Castle of Good Hope

ledger.note: 1652: the Dutch East India Company founds the Cape of Good Hope Waystation at Cape Town. Infobox 'Established: 6 April 1652' (the article's table gives 7 April 1652 for Jan van Riebeeck's start of office); the settlement was built 'in 1652 as a re-supply point'. The infobox names the Khoekhoe as predecessor.

region.text: the land ceded to the settlers round Table Bay

ledger.note: 1660: the Khoekhoe cede the land round the settlement. 'After the war, the natives ceded the land to the settlers in 1660.' The page names the war only through the link 'Khoikhoi-Dutch Wars' and gives no years for it.

1672: Commissioner Arnout van Overbeke buys the Cape territory. 'During a visit in 1672, the high-ranking Commissioner Arnout van Overbeke made a formal purchase of the Cape territory.' The page has the land already ceded in 1660; the extent of the purchase is not given.

region.text: Delagoa Bay, fort and factory Lijdzaamheid

ledger.note: April 1721: the Dutch govern Delagoa Bay from the Cape. 'In 1720, the Dutch East India Company built a fort and factory called Lijdzaamheid'; the settlement was 'since April 1721 governed by an opperhoofd (chief factor)' under the Dutch Cape Colony. A pirate occupation (Taylor) held it from April to 28 August 1722.
December 1730: the Dutch abandon Delagoa Bay. 'in December 1730 the settlement was abandoned.'

region.text: the inland districts added in Cliopatria's 1734 shape

ledger.note: 1734: the Cape grows to the Western Cape west of about 22 E (57,587 km2 in Cliopatria's shape). The page opened gives no 1734 event; recorded at the date of Cliopatria's step, as the bridge to the dated 1745 and 1780 events.

1745: a magistracy is set up at Swellendam. 'established a magistracy at Swellendam in 1745 and another at Graaff Reinet in 1786.' The page names the town, not the district's limits; the 120 km circle is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the interior added in Cliopatria's 1769 shape

ledger.note: 1769: the colony grows to 156,768 km2 in Cliopatria's shape (Western Cape and the south of the Northern Cape). The page opened dates no frontier before 1745 and 1780 (the Gamtoos River frontier is undated); recorded at the date of the shape.

region.text: the country up to the Great Fish River

ledger.note: November 1780: the Great Fish River becomes the eastern boundary. 'In November 1780, Van Plettenberg declared that the eastern border of the Cape colony was the entire length of the Great Fish river.' The Dutch Cape Colony page agrees ('the VOC agreed in 1780 to make the Great Fish River the boundary of the Cape'); Xhosa chiefdoms lay beyond. Region = the land Cliopatria adds in its 1788 shape.

1786: a magistracy at Graaff Reinet. 'established a magistracy at Swellendam in 1745 and another at Graaff Reinet in 1786.' Inside the Fish River boundary of 1780; the circle is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Graaff-Reinet district and the eastern frontier

ledger.note: 1795: the Graaff-Reinet district proclaims a republic. 'In 1795, after years of oppression by the Dutch East India Company (VOC), the inhabitants proclaimed a republic.' The Swellendam residents 'also did this' in 1795 (page); the Swellendam republic has no page of its own here (notes). Region = the eastern frontier districts of the 1794 shape (Eastern Cape part).

region.text: the Cape without the Graaff-Reinet district

ledger.note: 7 August 1795: the British occupy the Cape. Infobox 'First British occupation: 7 August 1795'; 'In 1795, after they launched an invasion of the Cape Colony in present-day Cape Town, the British occupied the Cape' (British fleet at Simon's Town, Dutch militia lost at Muizenberg). The Graaff-Reinet district is excluded: it stayed a republic until August 1796.

region.text: the Cape returned by Britain to the Batavian Republic

ledger.note: 1 March 1803: the Cape returns to Dutch rule. 'Britain ceded the Cape back to the Batavian Republic on 1 March 1803' (Peace of Amiens; the war resumed on 18 May 1803).

1803: the Cape becomes a colony of the Batavian Republic. The infobox gives 'Colony of the Batavian Republic (1803-1806)' after 'Supply station under Company rule (1652-1795)'; the Batavians had nationalised the VOC in 1796, its territories passed to the Republic in 1798 and the Company ceased in 1799. Governors De Mist (1803-1804) and Janssens (1804-1806/07; the page's two lists differ).

region.text: the Cape, lost to the British after Blaauwberg

ledger.note: January 1806: the British retake the Cape. 'In January 1806, the British occupied the colony for a second time after their victory at the Battle of Blaauwberg' (infobox 'British occupation: 8-18 January 1806').

1806: the Dutch Cape Colony ends. The land passes to the British Cape Colony; 'In 1814 the Dutch government formally ceded sovereignty over the Cape to the British' (infobox 'Official relinquishment: 13 August 1814').

wars.name: First Frontier War (First Xhosa War)

zones.text: the Zuurveld between the Great Fish and Sundays rivers

wars.outcome: Van Plettenberg declared the Great Fish River the eastern border in November 1780; Van Jaarsveld disbanded his commandos on 19 July 1781.
wars.note: 'The Dutch East India Company had demarcated the Great Fish River as the eastern boundary of the colony in 1779', though many settlers ignored it. No ledger contest: the page names no ground taken.

wars.name: British invasion of the Cape (Battle of Muizenberg)
wars.outcome: The British occupied the Cape from 7 August 1795 (infobox); the Dutch militia lost at Muizenberg.

wars.name: Battle of Blaauwberg (second British occupation)
wars.outcome: British victory; the Cape was occupied 8-18 January 1806 and ceded formally in 1814.

certainty.note: No frontier is given before 1745; the settled districts shade into Khoekhoe and trekboer country.
The Great Fish River line (declared November 1780) is a river line but the settlers and the Xhosa crossed it; the northern edge in the Karoo is approximate.

notes:
Merge: Cliopatria's 'Dutch Cape Colony' (1653-1795) and 'Napoleonic Batavia Republic' (1803-1805) share Wikidata Q4807130 and the Dutch Cape Colony article treats 1652-1806 as one colony (VOC rule to 1795, British occupation 1795-1803, Batavian rule 1803-1806), so there is one dossier under the earlier slug with both Names; no file napoleonic-batavia-republic.json is written. The land is the British Cape Colony's in 1796-1802 (ledger: loss 1795, gain 1803). Cliopatria's Wikipedia field is 'Dutch Cape Coast', a title that does not load; the article used is 'Dutch Cape Colony'.

Cliopatria problems: the 1653-1720 shape carries 12-14 cells in Senegal (Gorée / Cap-Vert; Dutch West India Company, lost to France in 1677) and the 1721-1733 shape 5 cells at Delagoa Bay (Dutch 1721-1730); both are corrected. The British Cape Colony row also draws the Cape in 1803-1805; the british-cape-colony dossier cuts those years. Cliopatria's 1805 is the last Batavian shape; the colony ended in January 1806, so a renderer working in whole years should give 1806 to the British.

Not settled: the extent of the 1734 and 1769 frontier steps (page silent); the Swellendam republic of 1795 (Graaff-Reinet page: 'also did this'; no page of its own opened, so no dates or events are entered); the Khoikhoi-Dutch Wars (1659-1660 and later; the Dutch page gives only 1660); Stellenbosch (1679) and Drakenstein (1687) not on the page. Pages: 'Dutch Cape Coast' failed to load (404).

State needing a dossier: Republic of Graaff-Reinet (written in this batch), Republic of Swellendam (1795), Xhosa chiefdoms (counterpart of the frontier).
